question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code to review pull requests and generate tests, and the project's root CLAUDE.md has grown into one 900-line file. It mixes testing conventions, API conventions, deployment checks and review criteria, and teammates often hit merge conflicts when they edit it. You want each topic kept in its own maintainable file, and every developer and the CI runner must still receive the instructions. Which change best achieves this?

options.text: Turn each topic into a separate slash command in .claude/commands/ that developers and the CI job invoke before each review.
options.reason: The .claude/commands/ directory holds slash commands that someone must invoke on demand; the guide names .claude/rules/ as the place for standing topic-specific rules.

options.text: Move each topic into the ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md file of the maintainer who owns that topic, so that each owner edits a separate file.
options.reason: User-level instructions in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md apply only to that user and are not shared through version control, so other teammates and the CI runner would lose them.

options.text: Split the content into focused topic files such as testing.md and api-conventions.md inside the project's .claude/rules/ directory.
options.reason: The guide names the .claude/rules/ directory as the place for topic-specific rule files, as an alternative to a monolithic CLAUDE.md, and project files reach everyone who clones the repository.

options.text: Keep the single CLAUDE.md file and add a table of contents with clear section headings so that each topic is easier to find and edit.
options.reason: The file stays monolithic, so the maintenance problem and the merge conflicts remain; the guide recommends splitting large CLAUDE.md files into topic files in .claude/rules/.
